misprints.note: Clearly a delta, with no breathing.
The print has ι where τ belongs.
The syllable 'τα' is repeated across the line break (περιεκτώτα-τατος).
Kept without breathing, as printed. The same happens with σπουδάζων, ουσα in 0017_03. It may be the book's normal style for endings, not an error.
Printed λ where τ belongs. The headword just before it is πτελέα.
The first κατα has no accent. On the next line it has one: κατὰ.

uncertain.note: The print shows 'a ,' with no visible full stop. It was probably 'a.,' with the stop missing.
No iota subscript can be seen under τῆ, although χώρᾳ clearly has one. I wrote it as printed. It may be a misprint for τῇ, or the subscript may just be faint.
The η has a breathing, a circumflex and a mark below. I read it as ᾗ, but it is small.
I read the mark on the α as a coronis: an acute on θἄτερον and none on θἀτέρου. The OCR had θᾶτερον and θάτέρου.
